meta.title: Beit Safafa family house, Mashrabiya House (2011)
meta.era: Contemporary: published on ArchDaily in October 2011 (the page states no completion year)

source.title: ArchDaily, 'The Mashrabiya House / Senan Abdelqader': ground floor plan (image 08fa, no scale bar), 1:200 longitudinal section (08fe) and 1:20 construction detail (08fc). Modelled: the west flat of the north block, ground floor.
source.license: Published plan, used only as a reference for dimensions

assumptions: Scale: the plan has no scale bar. Read at 47.5 px/m from the 1:200 section (storey levels 0.00/3.40/6.80/10.20 m = 33.8 px/m; grid D-A 14.59 m = 696 px on the plan), checked on beds (1.85-1.89 m) and the bathtub (1.79 m). Uncertainty about +-4 %: all lengths may be up to 0.3 m off.

Box: outer face of the west and north facades to the party-wall centre (east) and the outer face of the en-suite bathroom, which juts about 1.15 m past the bedrooms' south wall into the courtyard deck: 8.13 x 16.08 m. The deck strip beside it is labelled 'outside'. Clear height 3.10 m (3.40 m storey in the section minus a ~0.30 m slab).
The flat's half of the shared stair core is inside the box; it is labelled 'outside' so it is left out of the coverage shares. Its east side (the neighbour's half of the core) has no wall in the box.

The 1.8 x 3.0 m room between the stair and bath 2 has no label on the plan. Its four walls are hatched like the RC stair core and its door opens outward into the hall, as a mamad door does, so it is modelled as a protected room: mamad_20 walls, blast_door. At about 5.3 m2 it is below the 9 m2 mamad minimum and has no window, so it may be a store or a floor shelter instead; the concrete reading is the pessimistic one.
Safe-room door state: open (daily life: the steel door is usually left open). No window, so no window state.
Interior partitions: block_10 from the shared table (12 dB at 5 GHz). The draft's own 8 dB figure (which disagreed with 9 dB in other files) is dropped; no wall here sets loss_db.

North and west facades: the plan draws a ~0.3 m stone band (the mashrabiya screen) with a thin glazing line close behind it; the 1:20 detail shows the screen as stone blocks on a concrete beam with double glazing behind, no concrete wall. No table material is a perforated stone screen; stone_block (20 dB at 5 GHz) is the nearest and is used for the solid parts. Window sizes and sills are assumed (living: floor-to-ceiling sliding glass, as in the interior photos; bedrooms 1.4 x 1.5 m; bathrooms 0.6 x 0.6 m). The screen's perforations are not modelled. With the router inside, facade losses do not change the indoor shares.
No trisim behind the mashrabiya (the photos show none: the screen is the shading). The courtyard-side bedroom windows are given trisim with the slits open.
South walls to the courtyard deck (bedrooms and the jutting en-suite): drawn as a thin line (~0.12 m); material assumed Jerusalem stone on block (stone_block), windows assumed.

Party wall and stair-core walls: reinforced concrete 20 cm (concrete_20), from the hatching shared with the core; thickness drawn 0.15-0.2 m. The safe room's wall to the east flat's twin room is mamad_20.
Front door: steel entry door (pladelet), closed. Interior doors: hollow-core, open.
Fridge position assumed (the plan draws only the L-shaped counter); furniture otherwise from the plan.
Router: the ISP router in a communications cabinet in the hall beside the front door, 1.5 m high, 5 GHz, 20 dBm (no cabinet is drawn).
israeli_features: Jerusalem stone: a free-standing perforated stone mashrabiya screen wraps the facades (1:20 detail: stone blocks on a concrete beam)
several flats in one stone-screened house around a shared stair, a common Arab-Israeli family-building type (the source page does not say who the flats are for)
reinforced-concrete stair core with the flat's steel entry door (pladelet)
a small concrete room off the hall that is probably a protected space (mamad)
stone floor on a sand bed over the concrete slab (1:20 detail)
3.40 m storey height, generous for an Israeli flat
meta.notes: A four-room flat on the ground floor of a stone-screened house of several flats in Beit Safafa, Jerusalem, around a shared stair. The router by the front door covers the open living-kitchen-hall well, but every bedroom is behind at least one block wall and the parents' en-suite and bedroom 3 also sit behind wardrobes. The small concrete room beside the stair is treated as a safe room: with its door shut it gets almost no 5 GHz signal. The neighbouring flats share the stair core and the channels, which the model does not show.
